family: One fixed total language L with slices on all bit lengths N. If N<4 reject. Otherwise choose the largest integer w>=1 with n_w=2*w*2^w<=N, partition the first n_w bits into 2^w consecutive records of 2w bits, and accept iff these records are pairwise distinct; ignore the remaining N-n_w bits. A fixed deterministic polynomial-time pairwise-comparison evaluator decides L. Its NP verifier accepts exactly the empty witness when this evaluator accepts, with witness bound zero.
theorem: For this fixed language L in P, there exists N0 such that the minimum full-B2 gate count satisfies C_B2(L_N)>=N*(log2(log2 N))^2 for every integer N>=N0, with coefficient one and empty remainder. Consequently for each real A>0 there exists N_A such that C_B2(L_N)>=A*N for every integer N>=N_A. The supplied proofs establish these statements unconditionally by the distinctness tensor theorem over F_2, a constant-overhead simulation of unrestricted nonuniform Boolean circuits, and padding to all actual input lengths. The source theorem provides an existential fixed sigma>0; no numerical value of sigma is asserted.
